tools.name: kotoba_surface_status
tools.description: Is a Kotoba restriction PERMANENT or a backend that has not caught up? Reads lang/surface-status.edn and returns the entry's `disposition`: intentional-security-constraint and intentional-semantic-simplification are permanent; implemented-partial exists already; not-yet-implemented is a GAP, not a prohibition. Call this before concluding that Kotoba cannot express something, and before repeating any readiness claim from memory or from a document -- every such value in this workspace has gone stale at least once. The answer carries the authority's own `as-of` date; if it is old, the checkout is behind, not the language.

name.description: The invariant / surface entry to look up, e.g. 'bool-is-a-type-not-a-number'. Omit to list every entry with its disposition.

tools.outputContract: Hermes tool_result or tool_error; admitted is not executed.
tools.validation: source-extracted; execution-not-tested

tools.name: kotoba_capability_kits
tools.description: Which backends have QUALIFIED a Kotoba capability kit. Reads every resources/kotoba/lang/capability-kits/*.edn and returns each kit's `qualification` map verbatim. The key set differs per kit, so never summarise across kits, and `pending` records a measured refusal with a reason -- it does not mean nobody tried. Reading these with grep truncates silently on wrapped lines, which is why this tool exists.

kit.description: One kit id, e.g. 'ui-v1'. Omit for all kits.

tools.outputContract: Hermes tool_result or tool_error; admitted is not executed.
tools.validation: source-extracted; execution-not-tested

tools.name: kotoba_check
tools.description: Run `amu check` on one .kotoba file and return its verdict verbatim. IMPORTANT: `check` returning ok is NOT 'it works'. A value of the wrong type for document-bool passes check and fails at the value phase when the export is executed. Treat a passing check as 'the compiler admitted it', and run the export before saying more.

fresh.description: true bypasses the memo (same file closure + same amu -> served verdict) and re-runs amu check.

file.description: Path to the .kotoba file, relative to KOTOBA_WORKSPACE or absolute.

tools.outputContract: Hermes tool_result or tool_error; admitted is not executed.
tools.validation: source-extracted; execution-not-tested

tools.name: zap_scan
tools.description: Run a passive (non-intrusive) DAST scan of a target URL using the kotoba-lang/zap-proxy decision core (independent implementation; does not include or call OWASP ZAP). Checks security headers, cookie flags, and sensitive-info disclosure. Only targets recorded in zap_proxy_targets config are allowed — third-party hosts are refused. Returns a findings list with rule ids, severities, and evidence.

target.description: URL to scan, e.g. http://localhost:8080. Must be in zap_proxy_targets.

tools.outputContract: Native JSON string: refused/error or owner EDN findings/rules. A configured origin is not proof of caller authorization or target ownership.
tools.authority: caller-authorized owned target and page budget; scans require plugin target configuration; active requires allow_active as well; registration grants nothing
tools.validation: pinned Python AST literal schema extraction; no plugin execution, subprocess or scan performed

tools.name: zap_scan_active
tools.description: Run an ACTIVE (intrusive) DAST scan — injects detection payloads (SQLi, XSS, command injection, path traversal, CRLF) into query parameters. Only for targets explicitly allowed, and only with allow_active=true in the target's config entry. Detection is evidence-based (error reflection, marker arithmetic) — no destructive payloads. This is a defense-side diagnostic tool for hosts you control.

target.description: URL to scan. Must be in zap_proxy_targets with allow_active: true.

tools.outputContract: Native JSON string: refused/error or owner EDN findings/rules. A configured origin is not proof of caller authorization or target ownership.
tools.authority: caller-authorized owned target and page budget; scans require plugin target configuration; active requires allow_active as well; registration grants nothing
tools.validation: pinned Python AST literal schema extraction; no plugin execution, subprocess or scan performed

tools.name: zap_scan_rules
tools.description: List the zap-proxy rule registry: rule id, kind (passive/active), severity, and the IPA「ウェブ健康診断仕様」/ OWASP WSTG item each rule maps to. Use this to explain what a scan covers before running one.
tools.outputContract: Native JSON string: refused/error or owner EDN findings/rules. A configured origin is not proof of caller authorization or target ownership.

tools.description: Group Sentry data into Sentry-shaped issues: accepts an envelope (the body an SDK posts to /api/{project}/envelope/), event JSON (one object or an array) or a Sentry API /events/ response. Runs locally on the given text only: sends nothing, stores nothing, drops IP addresses, request headers, cookies and emails before grouping.

text.description: Envelope or event JSON text, at most 5 MiB of UTF-8.

project.description: Project slug to file every event under. Defaults to the envelope DSN's project, the event's project, or "mihari".

include_events.description: Also return each issue's events in Sentry /events/ shape. Default false.
